headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/data-flow coupling: gpt-engineer writes and executes code in a shared project directory, while whisper is a non-writing audio model with no direct bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a per-project directory and has no self-isolation by default; whisper is a CLI-style model with file input but no direct trust boundary or provenance tracking. A shared project directory can let attacker-controlled content from one side influence the other, though whisper itself does not ingest gpt-engineer outputs by default. Uncertainty about the exact bridge pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory or file set, injected instructions can cross the boundary.
IF gpt-engineer writes prompt-like text into files that whisper later reads as content, the pathway exists.
mitigations: Separate project directories per agent.
Disable automatic file re-ingestion between runs.
Review generated files before any downstream parsing.
Use a provenance tag or filename convention for machine-generated artifacts.
requires-engineering: add a trust boundary that prevents one agent from consuming the other's outputs as instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer can read and write the project directory and may send prompts to a configured model, while whisper is documented as local CLI-style and has no network egress or filesystem write. The pair does not show a shared sensitive-data class beyond generated code/audio, so leakage risk is limited unless the operator places secrets in the shared workspace. The lack of direct evidence keeps this low rather than none.
conditions: IF secrets or private source files are stored in the shared project directory, gpt-engineer can read them.
IF whisper is used on audio files containing sensitive speech, those contents may be exposed to the operator workflow.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Use separate directories for code and audio artifacts.
Redact sensitive audio before transcription.
Run both agents on least-privilege accounts.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls and secret scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has filesystem write and shell execution, while whisper has no write, no shell, and no subprocess capability. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct resource contention is minimal. The only shared mutable surface is the project directory, but whisper cannot modify it, making conflict unlikely.
conditions: IF whisper is wrapped by an external orchestrator that writes transcripts into the same directory, contention can appear.
IF gpt-engineer and an external wrapper both write the same filenames, collisions may occur.
mitigations: Use distinct output paths.
Serialize any wrapper writes.
Name outputs with unique run IDs.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same directory.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer can generate code and offer to run it, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. Whisper produces transcription output that could be fed into gpt-engineer as prompt material, creating a chain where one model's output becomes another's input without verification. Because neither profile shows built-in validation, the cascade is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF whisper transcripts are passed into gpt-engineer without human review, transcription errors can propagate into code.
IF gpt-engineer-generated code is executed automatically, downstream failures can cascade from bad outputs.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between transcription and code generation.
Require explicit approval before executing generated code.
Compare transcripts against source audio for critical tasks.
Limit gpt-engineer to draft-only mode.
requires-engineering: add automated validation for transcript-to-code pipelines.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both are open-source with no requested OAuth scopes. The main compliance concern is operator-managed data handling: gpt-engineer touches generated source code and whisper touches audio/speech, so mixing regulated audio with code workflows could create policy gaps. The evidence is sparse, so this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated audio or personal data is transcribed by whisper and then stored in the code workspace, policy scope may expand.
IF the operator requires residency or retention guarantees, neither profile documents them.
mitigations: Keep regulated audio out of the code workspace.
Document retention for transcripts and generated code.
Separate storage locations by data class.
Review vendor policy requirements before deployment.
requires-engineering: add compliance controls for retention and residency.
